reason: No supplied end-to-end result establishes a speedup for these proposals. I rank the output-store reorder first because it keeps the FP32 reduction and data layout unchanged, so its correctness risk is relatively low; any locality benefit remains unverified. The 320-byte scratch stride is a distinct, testable layout change, but cache indexing is unknown and the earlier 272-byte variant did not promote. n512_fast_path and assembly_audit specify the same TB descriptor and A conversion, so they are aliases; rank them together and test at most once. panel_packing uses TB with a different timed B conversion. TA and TT add costly conversions, while transpose_fusion and a_transpose require more complex layout work; their net effects are unknown. Historical scores are noisy and do not establish causes or benefits for these candidates.
